claims.nodeLabel: Burlison UAP Records Disclosure Amendment, FY2027 NDAA
claims.text: The House adopted Burlison's UAP records disclosure amendment as part of the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act in July 2026; it would require agencies to identify, preserve and transfer UAP records to the National Archives on a statutory timeline and establish an independent UAP Records Review Board with Senate-confirmed members and subpoena authority.
In July 2026 the House approved a Burlison amendment creating a framework for UAP records disclosure.

The House adopted Burlison's Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act amendment to the FY2027 NDAA on 23 July 2026; it creates a UAP Records Review Board with Senate-confirmed members and subpoena authority and extends disclosure obligations to government contractors.
The amendment requires agencies to identify, preserve and transfer covered UAP records to a permanent National Archives collection under a statutory timeline.

claims.nodeLabel: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA
claims.text: This was the first year Burlison's UAP disclosure amendment advanced to a House floor vote; a similar proposal failed to advance in the previous year's defence bill cycle. The measure now goes to the Senate.

edges.note: The House framework must survive conference against a Senate reported bill (S. 4784, S. Rept. 119-127) containing zero UAP provisions - the second consecutive cycle in which the subject is absent from the Senate base text. The 2023 precedent is that the eminent-domain and review-board provisions were stripped in conference.

edges.label: Would impose statutory transfer timelines on the NARA collection

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

b.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters

edges.label: Statutory backstop for an executive release programme
edges.note: Burlison's own release frames the amendment as supporting PURSUE; structurally it cures each of PURSUE's defects - no timeline, no subpoena power, no reach to contractors, no Senate-confirmed decision-maker.
